title.narrative: Well coordinated Labour migration management system established/ strengthened

description.narrative: Labour migration is vital to Kenya’s economy, with remittances contributing significantly to GDP. Yet, migrant workers; especially women and low-skilled labourers, remain vulnerable to exploitation, trafficking, and abuse. In response, the ILO is supporting the Government of Kenya to establish a comprehensive, rights-based labour migration governance system that aligns with national development goals and safeguards migrant rights. The strategy aims to strengthen Kenya’s regulatory and institutional frameworks by addressing human trafficking, forced labour, and child labour risks, particularly in high-flow sectors. Efforts include reviewing policies and aligning them with international labour standards, notably ILO Conventions No. 97 and No. 143. The programme also integrates gender responsiveness to ensure equal protection for male and female migrant workers. Beneficiaries include migrant workers in vulnerable positions, the National Employment Authority (NEA), trade unions, employers’ organizations, and civil society actors. The programme promotes stronger coordination, capacity-building, and development of fair recruitment and placement mechanisms, contributing to decent work outcomes in both Kenya and destination countries. Expected results include enhanced institutional capacities, improved protection systems for migrant workers, and more coherent stakeholder coordination. These efforts contribute to safer, more orderly labour migration and advance Kenya’s commitments under the Decent Work Country Programme (DWCP), particularly in promoting decent work, extending social protection, and upholding international labour standards.
